audit.whatIsWrong: Both the content win[] chart and the full-layer phases give Graves Levels 1, 2 and 3 and call Levels 4-5 'Skill', while the packet levelChart reads Skill / Skill / Skill / Graves / Skill / Graves / Skill and the content whys describe exactly the packet order.
audit.why: whys[0] 'Both of you are weak at level 1', whys[1] 'Neither of you is fully online yet' and whys[2] 'it's a genuine trade race' are all Skill stages; whys[3] 'let you win extended melee trades' is the Graves stage. The enum charts were left on Graves-boilerplate and contradict the prose sitting next to them.
audit.corrected: Both charts set to Skill / Skill / Skill / Graves / Skill / Graves / Skill, ratings 5,5,5,7,5,7,5 from the Graves side. Difficulty 5.5/10 and the EVEN tag are correct against 48.78% over 82 games — left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why describes Collateral Damage generically ('an execute and a disengage knockback') without noting that Depth Charge arrives on the same level, and phases[5] gives the generic 'removes half bars' line rather than the lethality-vs-armour-stacking reason the first item actually spikes here.
audit.why: Level 6 is a mutual spike: Graves' R is 100s at rank 1, Depth Charge is 120s at rank 1 and is an unmissable single-target lock. The first-item window is Graves' cleanest because lethality outpaces Nautilus' early armour stacking; by two items his durability has caught up. The existing text records none of this.
audit.corrected: phases[4] rewritten as the mutual all-in decided by who whiffs first; phases[5] and [6] rewritten to the lethality-versus-stacking-tank timeline.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'early' says 'the blind only cuts auto-attacks, and Nautilus locks you with abilities'; report[10].t says 'Your W smoke blinds tower dives'; phases[6].why says 'smoke-screen blinds'.
audit.why: Graves' Smoke Screen is not a blind. Riot's text: 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' It is a nearsight plus an impact slow — the kit flags are projectile, slow, zone with no blind. The conclusion the text draws (don't count on W to stop his CC) is right, but it is reached through a mechanic that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Describe it as cutting sight range and slowing on impact — that is also why it does nothing about a landed hook.
sources: ownerKit W Riot text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow is never named or explained, and Dredge Line's terrain behaviour is absent.
audit.why: Riot: 'Nautilus' first Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly' — that root is why standing in his melee range is a lockdown regardless of whether the hook is up, and it is the CC that starts his chain when the hook is down. Separately, Riot's Q text says 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it', so a whiffed hook is not always a whiffed engage — he can wall-hook to reposition. The 'dodge the hook and the lane is free' line needs the first fact attached.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now names Staggering Blow as the reason melee range is a lockdown; the terrain-hook is recorded here as a caveat rather than crammed into a length-capped field.
sources: enemyKit P and Q Riot text

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line is repeatedly called the clock but its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: 14/13/12/11/10s is a long window on a champion whose whole lane threat is that one button. 'Fourteen free seconds' is actionable; 'dodge it and the lane is free' is not.
audit.corrected: Real number added to dosFull[0].d and phases[3].why.

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: Neither has a kit yet, but Dredge Line plus his auto-root passive is the scariest button here. Just farm.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: Still a button short each — trade short and never give him a straight line for Dredge Line's 1150-unit range.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: Your shell spread arrives with his hook-root-Riptide chain — a trade race, so weave rather than commit.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Dredge Line (Hook); your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: True Grit stacks and a held E charge win the extended trade; a whiffed Dredge Line leaves him 14 seconds without an engage.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Collateral Damage and Depth Charge land together — a mutual all-in decided by whoever whiffs their button first.

edits.before: First item spike — the point-blank Q-AA-E-AA pattern now removes half bars. Force fights near walls.
edits.after: First item is your cleanest window — lethality punches through before his armor stacking catches up.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: His tankiness eats your burst while the hook-into-knockup chain stays lethal — skirmish, don't duel him.

edits.before: His only real engage — dodge it and the lane is free. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Dredge Line is his only real engage — dodge it and you own the next 14 seconds.

edits.before: That’s Nautilus’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His first attack on you roots — Staggering Blow makes melee range a lockdown.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W cuts vision on a dive and slows the arrival — drop it on the jungler and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin-flip — neither of you has the kit yet, but his Dredge Line hook plus the passive auto-root is the scariest single button in the lane, so never walk in a straight line at him. The instant you have E and Q (2-3) you can play your game: Quickdraw in for the point-blank 4-shell spread, drop End of the Line, and dash back out on your second E charge before his hook can reel you. Your Smoke Screen is for disengage and zoning, not for stopping his CC — the blind only cuts auto-attacks, and Nautilus locks you with abilities, so don't expect to smoke your way out of a landed hook.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin-flip — neither of you has the kit yet, but his Dredge Line hook plus the Staggering Blow auto-root is the scariest single button in the lane, so never walk in a straight line at him. The instant you have E and Q (2-3) you can play your game: Quickdraw in for the point-blank 4-shell spread, drop End of the Line, and dash back out on your second E charge before his 14-second hook can reel you. Smoke Screen is for disengage and zoning, not for stopping CC — it reduces sight range and slows on impact, it does not blind, so a landed hook still chains through it.

notes: Suspect name 'Your Collateral Damage' in whys[4] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Collateral Damage is Graves' real R name per the kit; nothing to fix there. The level chart was wrong in BOTH layers in the same way and in the same direction (Graves handed Levels 1-3 he does not own), while the content whys already described the packet order correctly — all seven rows proposed together as one atomic group. Smoke Screen was again described as a blind in three places; corrected against Riot's text, which says only that it reduces sight range and slows on impact. Kit flag caution: the brief's derived flags put 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' on Graves' Q, but Riot's description says the shell 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain' — it interacts with terrain, it does not create any. I removed the 'wall-bounce' framing from phases[2] rather than repeat it, and asserted no terrain-creation anywhere. One genuine mechanic I recorded in the audit but could not fit into a length-capped field: Riot's Dredge Line text says 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it', so a hook that misses you can still be used as a wall-dash — the repeated 'dodge it and the lane is free' framing slightly overstates the reward. Mirror file nautilus__graves did not exist at audit time.
